recent_posts.title: My Tips for Designing Better User Experiences
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of UX design decisions made while building Mission Control, a developer tool for vibe coders and agentic coding workflows. Key principles covered include defining your target audience, optimizing for core workflows, using hotkeys for power users, keeping UI language simple for non-coders, and only surfacing frequently-used actions in the main UI. The author also discusses tradeoffs around features like git worktrees and pull request management, ultimately deciding to exclude them to reduce complexity for the target audience of solo vibe coders.

recent_posts.title: AI is killing programming tutorials and developer content creation
recent_posts.summary: A developer reacts to WebDev Simplified's video about AI's impact on programming content creation. Key points: programming tutorial views are collapsing as audiences shift to AI content, YouTube ad revenue for educational channels is unsustainable ($31K/year for 2M subscribers), AI tools like Claude Code are replacing the need to watch tutorials, and there's a concerning feedback loop where AI trains on human-created content while simultaneously making that content less profitable to produce. The author argues AI coding tools are genuinely transformative (not a fad like crypto), advocates for developers to build foundational knowledge before relying on AI, and warns that software engineer salaries may decline as AI lowers the cost of building software.

AI plugin that automates git commits and pull request descriptions
recent_posts.summary: A developer showcases a custom AI-powered plugin called 'Agentic System Labs Essentials' that automates the pull request workflow. The tool analyzes staged changes, groups them into logical commits, proposes a branch name, generates a descriptive PR description, links relevant GitHub issues, suggests reviewers, and auto-tags labels. The demo walks through installing the plugin, running the 'ship PR' skill, reviewing the AI-generated commit plan, and confirming the final pull request on GitHub. The plugin requires the GitHub CLI to be authenticated and is open source.

recent_posts.title: Practical uses of GPT Image 2 for web projects and side projects
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of OpenAI's GPT Image 2 model, showcasing practical use cases including generating open graph images from website URLs, extracting and fixing perspective on phone screenshots, creating transparent cutouts, and redesigning landing page hero sections. The author demonstrates integrating Image 2 into side projects like an icon generator and an AI clip studio, highlighting the model's text rendering quality and image editing capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Understanding Opus 4.7 Effort Level
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of how effort levels work in Claude's Opus 4.7 model, based on a Reddit post. Key points: effort is a behavioral signal controlling adaptive reasoning depth, tool call appetite, response length, and agentic autonomy — not a strict token budget. Opus 4.7 defaults to 'extra high' effort on all plans including Pro, while Opus 4.6 defaulted to 'medium' on Pro/Max plans, explaining why some users perceived a quality drop. Low effort Opus 4.7 roughly equals medium effort Opus 4.6. Importantly, context quality can matter more than effort level — a well-contextualized low-effort prompt often beats a poorly-contextualized max-effort one. Opus 4.7 also uses 10–35% more tokens than 4.6, so matching effort level to task complexity (e.g., Sonnet low for simple tasks, Opus max for architecture/security) is important for managing token costs.

top_posts.title: This is the software engineering mindset you need
top_posts.summary: In software engineering, developing a mindset to break down large, complex problems into smaller, manageable parts is crucial. Gaining experience in solving various smaller tasks helps build confidence and skills, making it easier to tackle larger projects over time. The key to growth is continuous practice and learning from solving small, distinct problems, which eventually enables solving bigger challenges more efficiently.

top_posts.title: This is the coolest side project I've worked on
top_posts.summary: A project is described that allows users to create videos based on written stories, focusing initially on scary stories but aiming to expand to any type of story. The process involves breaking the story into segments, generating AI-powered images for each segment using OpenAI and Replicate, and then creating a video by stitching these segments together with Lambda functions. The project also aims to include features like background music and other enhancements. Future improvements are being considered, such as using GPU-optimized EC2 instances or rewriting code in faster programming languages like Go or Rust.

top_posts.title: AI coding tools are transforming software development in 2026
top_posts.summary: AI-powered coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and GPT models are fundamentally changing software development. LLMs can now generate entire features across dozens of files, write tests, and even build complete applications with minimal manual coding. The shift moves developers from writing code by hand to prompt engineering and context engineering—providing documentation and requirements that guide AI agents. Front-end development and manual UI coding are becoming commoditized as AI handles component generation and styling. Developers need to focus on higher-level skills like software architecture, system design, and diversify into project management and communication. Autonomous coding systems can now run overnight, implementing features and fixing bugs with minimal human intervention.

top_posts.title: My side project now has 4 paying customers
top_posts.summary: An overview of a side project called the Scary Story Generator, which now has four paying customers. The project utilizes AI for generating story prompts, images, and videos, including specific features like TikTok shorts and customizable story segments. Despite certain performance optimization needs, the project has earned $25 in gross revenue and aims to expand beyond Halloween by rebranding for general video creation.

top_posts.title: A senior developer reflects on losing the joy of coding to AI tools
top_posts.summary: A veteran web developer with 13 years of experience shares his personal struggle with the loss of joy in coding since AI tools like Claude Code and Cursor became dominant. He reflects on how agentic coding has replaced the satisfaction of hands-on problem solving, discusses the anxiety of managing multiple AI agents, and questions the future of his career and YouTube channel. He also touches on the difficult job market, the rise of vibe coding by non-developers, and where experienced developers might still have an edge — in deep technical knowledge or business/marketing skills.
